 Judgement

This claim petition is filed by the petitioner under Section 166 of Indian Motor Vehicles Act, seeking
compensation for the injuries sustained by him in a road traffic accident.

2.  The case of the petitioner is as follows:
On 7.8.2008 at about 10.30 p.m., the petitioner was proceeding in TVS Moped bearing Reg.No.KA02EV7331 on Solur Circle, at that time all of a sudden one Auto bearing Reg.No.KA06A9862 came in high speed in rash and negligent manner and dashed against the TVS, result of which he fell down and suffered grievous injuries.
Immediately he was shifted to Govt. Hospital, Kudur for first aid treatment and then shifted to M.S.Ramaiah Hospital, Bangalore wherein admitted as an inpatient from 08.08.2008 to 29.08.2008.

He spent sum of Rs.2, 50,000/
towards treatment, medicines, conveyance and nourishment .

Prior to the accident,
he was working as a Coolie and earning Rs.200/per day . He has suffered pain and sufferings, permanent disability, loss of income, loss of future income and other pecuniary and non pecuniary damages.
3. In spite of due service of notice, the 2nd Respondent remained absent from appearing before the Court, hence, vide order dt.26.3.11 he was placed ex parte.

4. After due service of notice, the 1 st Respondent has engaged the service of Counsel and got filed a detailed Written Statement and also called upon the claimants to strict proof of the averments made at Col.Nos.1 to 22 of the claim petition.

It is the contention of the 1 st Respondent, the policy was in force as on the date of incident, but liability if any is subject to the terms and conditions of the policy.
5. It is the contention of the 1st Respondent that accident in question occurred only due to the negligence on the part of claimant and denied the involvement of offending vehicle and negligence on the part of the diver of the offending vehicle.
It is the contention of the 1st Respondent that the amount claimed by the claimant is exorbitant and without any basis.
Hence urged to reject the Claim Petition.

6. On the strength of the above pleadings, I have framed the following:
ISSUES 1.Whether the Claimant proves that he sustained grievous injuries in RTA that occurred on 7.8.2008 at about 10.30 p.m. while riding TVS Moped bearing Gangadhar vs B A G Ins Co Ltd on 15 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/116173973/
2 Reg.No.KA02EV7331 in front of Mangalamma Vegetable Shop, Kudur Main Road, Kudur due to rash and negligent driving of an Auto bearing Reg.
No.KA06A9862 by its driver?
2. Whether the Claimant is entitled for compensation as claimed ?

If so, to what amount and from whom ?
3

. What order or Award?
7.
In order to substantiate the case made out by the petitioner, the petitioner got himself examined as P.W.1 and two witnesses has been examined as P.W.2 and Pw.3 and got marked Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.20.
Thereafter, the petitioner closed his side evidence.

8. In order to rebut the evidence so placed on record by the petitioner, the respondent no.1 has examined its Legal executive as RW.1 and examined one witness as RW.2 and got marked documents as per Ex.R1 to 6.
Thereafter, respondent no.1 closed their side evidence.
9. After hearing the arguments this Tribunal has passed judgment and award dated 13032012.

Aggrieved by the correctness of the order passed by this court fixing liability on the respondent no 1 and 2 as jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation amount with interest within 30 days from the date of award.

(Subject to dismissal of MVC No.273/2010 on the file of MACT,
Ramanagara by the claimant), the respondent no.1 has preferred appeal in M.F.A.No:8805/2012 (MVI) before the Hon'ble High court.
The Honb'le High Court was pleased to remand the matter to the tribunal by setting aside the judgment and award passed by this court with direction to decide the petition afresh.
10. After remand of the case, the Senior Executive of the respondent no 1 company was examined as Rw.3 and got marked documents as Ex.R7 and R8.
Sri Ravi Prakash B.GMRD department is examined as RW.4 and got marked document at Ex.R9 and 10, thereafter matter was posted for arguments.
11. Heard the arguments.
The respondent no. 1 has filed written argument on their behalf.
Perused the materials placed on record.

12. My findings on the above Issues are as here under:
Issue No.1: In the Negative Issue No.2: In the Negative Issue No.3: As per final order below, For the following: REASONS 13.
Issue No.1 :
Now before adverting to discuss on issue no 1 it is better to have glance on the previous proceedings as to what are all the things that had transpired in the case.

The petitioner alleged to be the victim of the road traffic accident filed the present petition alleging that on 7/8/2008 at about 10.30 p.m., he was proceeding on TVS Moped on Solur Circle at that time all of a Gangadhar vs B A G Ins Co Ltd on 15 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/116173973/
3 sudden on Auto came in a high speed and in a rash and negligent manner dashed against TVS , as a result of which he fell down and suffered grievous injuries.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: This tribunal after holding full fledged trial by relying upon ExP1 to ExP6 i.e FIR, complaint, statement, Mahazar IMV report and charge sheet had held that the accident had taken place because of the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle and hence held that insurance company is liable to pay the compensation.
14. Aggrieved by the judgment and decree passed by this court, the respondent no.1/Insurance company preferred appeal before the hon'ble High court in MFA NO 8805 of 2012 .

Before the hon'ble appellate court the appellant filed application under Order 41 Rule 27 CPC and produced MLC register extract of M.S Ramaiah Hospital Bengaluru where in on 8/8/2008 as per the entry it is mentioned as " RTA bike hit to the tree and fall from bike at about 10.30 P.M at Kudure - Magadi".

Having regard to the additional documents produced by the appellant and in the light of the complaint that was given after 11 days of the accident, the Hon'ble appellate court has set aside the award dated 13.3.2012 and remanded the matter back to this court for fresh consideration by giving opportunity to both the parties to adduce evidence.
15. After remand back of the case, though sufficient opportunity was given to the petitioner, he has not taken any steps to adduce either oral or documentary evidence.

On the other hand the respondent no 1 has adduced the evidence of two witnesses as Rw3 and Rw4 and got marked additional documents as Ex.R7 to 10.
16.
In order to prove the issue on hand, the Claimant by name Sri.Gangadhar has sworn to an affidavit and got examined as Pw1.

In order to establish the fact of rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle, the Claimant has produced the Certified copies of FIR, complaint, statement,
mahazar, IMV report and the charge sheet as per Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.4, Ex.P.6 and Ex.P.5, respectively.

17. On the basis of the complaint lodged by the sister of petitioner, FIR came to be lodged against the driver of the alleged offending vehicle and after investigation charge sheet was filed against him.

The respondent no 2 who is the owner of the offending vehicle has remained exparte and there by not contested the case.
18.

As observed supra the respondent no 1 has seriously disputed the very involvement of offending vehicle in the accident and also much argued about the delayed complaint lodged by the sister of the petitioner and submitted that the petitioner, his relatives, the owner and driver of the offending vehicle in collusion with the jurisdictional Police have falsely implicated the offending vehicle in the accident even though offending vehicle was not involved in the accident hence only there was delay of 11 days in lodging the complaint.
The learned counsel for respondent no 1 has relied much upon the ExR8/Ex. R10 i.e the MLC register of M.S Ramaiah Hospital.

As per the own case of the petitioner soon after the accident he was shifted to Kudur Government hospital and after taking primary treatment he was shifted to M.S Ramaiah hospital on the same date of accident and he was in M.S Ramaiah hospital as inpatient from 7/8/2008 to 29/8/2008.
If complaint and FIR is perused, though the accident in question has occurred on 7/8/2008 at 10.00 p.m but complaint came to be lodged on 18/8/2008 at 1.00 p.m.
Complaint was lodged by the sister of petitioner.

In Gangadhar vs B A G Ins Co Ltd on 15 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/116173973/
4 the complaint and FIR it is stated that since complainant was engaged in providing treatment to the petitioner there was delay in lodging the complaint.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 19. At the cost of repetition, the respondent no 1 has seriously disputed the involvement of offending vehicle in the accident and categorically contended that the petitioner has sustained injuries when he was proceeding in his motor cycle as rider in rash and negligent manner and hit to the tree result of which he fell down and sustained injuries, however subsequently with an intention to make an unlawful gain from the respondent no1 with the help of second respondent falsely implicated the alleged offending vehicle and foisted false case by twisting the entire episode to suit the need of the hour and in active collusion and connivance with the police by creating false crime records a make believe story .

20. In the light of the objection statement of the respondent no 1, the evidence placed on record by them and the line of argument canvassed by the learned counsel for respondent no 1, if the materials placed on record is carefully scrutinized, as observed supra it is not in dispute that after the alleged accident the petitioner has taken first aid treatment at Kudur Hospital and thereafter on the same date of accident he was shifted to M.S Ramaiah hospital.

The petitioner has produced the wound certificate, inpatient bills and case sheet of MS Ramaiah hospital to prove the nature of injuries sustained by him, the nature of treatment given to him and the amount spent by him for the treatment etc but he has not produced MLC register either of Kudur hospital or of MS Ramaiah hospital.

It is relevant to state here that though the respondent no1 before the hon'ble Appellate court had produced MLC register of MS Ramaiah hospital as additional document and thereby raised serious objection regarding the cause for injury sustained by the petitioner and even though hon'ble high court remanded back the case to this court to decide the case afresh by giving opportunity to the respective parties to lead their evidence but petitioner has not taken any steps to prove the contention taken by them by producing the MLC register of Kudur hospital to let the court know what is the entry made at first in point of time in the MLC register of Kudur hospital regarding the alleged history of accident.

If the materials placed on record is perused, from the date of remand of the case till the case is posted for argument, the respondent no1 had taken all the possible steps constantly to secure the MLC register of Kudur hospital by issuing process through court, by hand and RPAD.

As Medical officer, Government Hospital Kudur, Ramangar District had refused to receive the hand summons and even having served the RPAD the medical officer of Kudur Government hospital failed to appear before the court and produce the MLC register, this court at the submission of respondent no1 even had issued bailable warrant against him.

In spite of that he did not appear and produce the document, finally this court by rejecting the prayer of respondent no1 to reissue process against to the Medical officer Government hospital Kudur, closed the respondents evidence and proceeded to hear the argument .
Hence respondent no 1 has taken all possible steps to secure the medical records of Kudur Hospital.
21. If the wound certificate and case sheet issued from M.S Ramaiah hospital is perused, where in the alleged history of injury is mentioned as "RTA".
In none of the medical documents referred by the petitioner, the involvement of offending vehicle is mentioned.
As per the very contents of the complaint, soon after the alleged accident the driver of the offending vehicle sped away from the spot along with vehicle.

But in the complaint the registration number of the alleged offending Gangadhar vs B A G Ins Co Ltd on 15 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/116173973/
5 vehicle is mentioned.

entities.text: Gangadhar vs B A G Ins Co Ltd
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is no where forthcoming who has given the registration number of the alleged offending vehicle to the complainant so as to mention the registration number in the complaint.
If the address of the driver of offending vehicle is perused, he is the resident of Kudur Village Magadi Taluk which itself is the address of petitioner.
It means both the driver of alleged offending vehicle and petitioner are hails from same village.

If ExR8/ Ex.R10 i.e MLC register of MS Ramaiah hospital is perused, where in the alleged history of injury is mentioned as "RTA bike hit the tree and fall from bike at about 10.30 p.m on 7/8/2008 at Kudur Magadi Taluk''.
At the cost of repetition it is soon after the accident, after taking first aid treatment at Kudur Hospital the petitioner was shifted to M.S Ramaih hospital.
If ExR8 is carefully perused at the time of petitioner was shifted to MS Ramaiah hospital he was conscious and oriented.
The petitioner has not placed any contra evidence to the evidence of respondent no1 to say that the entry in the ExR8 is wrong and that ExR8 cannot be relied upon.

The petitioner could have examined the medical officer of Kudur hospital and could have produced the MLC register of Kudur hospital, but as observed supra he has not taken even minimum pain to secure the said documents for the reason best known to him.

Even though respondent no1 has seriously disputed the manner of accident and the involvement of offending vehicle in the accident, the petitioner thought it not necessary to examine any of the eye witness to the accident to substantiate his contention.

It is true that petitioner has examined Dr.
Gopalappa HM the medical officer MS Ramaiah hospital as Pw2 and from whom inpatient case sheet and X rays are got marked as ExP15 to ExP18 but nothing is elicited from his mouth regarding the alleged history of accident mentioned in the medical records.

If evidence of Pw2 is perused ,
except producing case sheet and X ray he has not stated anything regarding the treatment given to the Pw1 for the injuries sustained in the RTA.
The Pw2 pleaded ignorance of the contents of the medical documents.

22. The petitioner has examined Pw3 Dr. B Ramesh non treated doctor to prove the disability suffered by the petitioner, but when the very involvement of offending vehicle in the accident so also the alleged history of injury itself is in dispute, unless and until said two material points are proved any amount of evidence given by Pw3 would not help the petitioner in proving his case.

If entry in the ExR8 is relied upon it can be said without any hesitation that since petitioner has sustained injury due to his negligence of hit against the tree and fall down on the road, there was delay of 11 days in lodging the complaint.

If really the petitioner has sustained injury in RTA due to hit against the motor cycle by auto rickshaw, then even if registration number of offending vehicle is not mentioned in the MLC at least involvement of three wheeler vehicle would have been mentioned and on registering the MLC the hospital authority would have given police intimation to the jurisdictional police and Jurisdictional police would have recorded the statement of the petitioner by approaching him in the hospital.

As rightly argued by the learned counsel for respondent no.1, ExR8 was maintained immediately after the alleged accident well before the police documents came in to existence and the medical documents raised first in point of time prevail over the police documents.

23. The learned counsel for respondent no1 at this juncture has referred judgment in MFA No 2006 /2010 (MV) c/w 1763/2010 (MV) between S.T Deepu V/s The New India Assurance company Limited where in the hon'ble High court has observed that 'Since it is allegedly a medico legal case,
the need for the petitioner himself visiting the police station for lodging the complaint does not merits acceptance in as much as police would be visiting the injured in the hospital itself, therefore Gangadhar vs B A G Ins Co Ltd on 15 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/116173973/
6

entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: Gangadhar vs B A G Ins Co Ltd on 15 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: the explanation that delay in lodging the FIR is because of hospitalization becomes doubtful.

24. In M.F.A No 794/2009 (MV) Between M/S Bajaj Allianz General Insurance Company Ltd /
Nagamma and Ors, referring to the facts in the said case which is similar to the present case has observed that "the doctors evidence which is immediately after the incident could be considered to ascertain the incident and the medical documents show that accident was due to fall from the bicycle hence claimant is not entitled to any compensation".

entities.text: Bajaj Allianz General Insurance Company Ltd
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: 25. In the present case also as observed supra if the case of the petitioner were to be true, certainly hospital authorities would have given intimation to the concerned police station and certainly the police would have visited the hospital and would have recorded the statement of the injured or his attendant.
Hence delay in lodging the complaint and the Ex.R8 which falsify the case of the petitioner so far as involvement of the alleged offending vehicle in the accident.

26. The learned counsel for the petitioner referring the IMV report and the nature of damage caused to the alleged offending vehicle and also the charge sheet field against the driver of the alleged offending vehicle has submitted that if really the offending vehicle is not involved in the accident there is no possibility of sustaining damage to the said vehicle and that jurisdictional Police after investigation have filed charge sheet against the driver of offending vehicle, hence the court will have to presume that accident had occurred in the manner stated by the claimant.
27. If the IMV report as at Ex.P6 is perused, the alleged offending vehicle was inspected through RTO on 21/8/2008 i.e after lapse of nearly 14 days from the date of accident.
As per ExP6 the centre right side body of alleged offending vehicle was damaged.
As per the case of petitioner there was head on collusion between the two vehicles.

If really the alleged offending vehicle by coming from opposite direction in rash and negligent manner hit against to the two wheeler of the petitioner,
then some amount of damage would have been caused on the front side of the offending vehicle but not on the right centre body of the alleged vehicle.
Further the alleged offending vehicle was inspected after lapse of nearly 14 days from the date of alleged accident.
Hence there is every possibility of the said vehicle get damaged for some other reason.

Hence merely on the ground that some minor damage found in the alleged offending vehicle that too after lapse of nearly 14 days from the date of accident the court cannot come to the conclusion that the alleged offending vehicle is involved in the accident.

28. So far as the charge sheet filed by the investigation officer against the driver of the alleged offending vehicle is concerned, as observed supra the medical documents raised first in point of time prevails over the police documents.
Hence court has to rely upoj ExR8 instead of charge sheet.
29. In a judgment rendered in MFA No 2829/2009 (MV) Manju / Mathue KP and ors it was held that filing of charge sheet under section 173(5) Cr.P.C may give rise to a presumption.
However that is not decisive on the issue.

If the court finds evidence adduced by parties and material placed by parties are sufficient to hold that charge sheet filed by police is a fabricated document, the claim petition cannot be sustained.
The law is fairly well settled that court has to consider documents filed under section 173(5) Cr.P.C in additional to the evidence adduced by parties before tribunal.

The Gangadhar vs B A G Ins Co Ltd on 15 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/116173973/
7 court should not be swayed away by the documents filed under section 173(5) Cr.P.C.

entities.text: Gangadhar vs B A G Ins Co Ltd on 15 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The owner cum rider of the vehicle involved in the accident had benevolently lent his name and vehicle to fabricate charge sheet to lend support to the case of claimant.

In the circumstances jurisdictional Police did not have any difficulty to fabricate the documents and file charge sheet against the driver,
who in fact had readily obliged.
In the circumstances, the insurance company cannot be made liable to pay compensation in a claim petition filed on the basis of fabricated documents.

30. If the entire materials placed on record is carefully perused in the light of the observation made in the aforesaid judgment, it can be said without any hesitation that there is no nexus between the injury sustained by the petitioner and the offending vehicle.

When alleged offending vehicle is not at all involved in the accident the question of rash and negligent act on the part of the driver of the alleged offending vehicle in causing the alleged accident does not arise.
Hence issue no1 is answered in the Negative.
31. Issue no 2 :

When the very involvement of offending vehicle in the accident is not proved and when the petitioner has failed to prove that he has sustained injury in the Road traffic accident,
instead the respondent no1 has proved that petitioner has sustained injury due to his self negligence by hitting to the tree under such circumstances he is not entitled for compensation .
Hence issue no 2 is answered in the negative.
32. Issue no 3 : In view of the findings given on issue no1 and 2 this court proceeds to pass the following:' ORDER The Claim Petition filed U/s.166 of M.V.ACT is dismissed.
Draw Award Accordingly.
(Typed by me in Laptop , corrected and then pronounced by me in open court, on this the 15th day of April 2024.)
(ROOPASHRI) XXII Addl., SCJ & ACMM., Bengaluru.

Hence issue no 2 is answered in the negative.
32. Issue no 3 : In view of the findings given on issue no1 and 2 this court proceeds to pass the following:' ORDER The Claim Petition filed U/s.166 of M.V.ACT is dismissed.
Draw Award Accordingly.
